# Loment 0.1.4.5 QuickFix

A patch on top of [0.1.4.5](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/releases/tag/v0.1.4.5). The toolchain
binaries in this package are **byte for byte the same** as that release's; what changed is the
Windows **installer**.

## What was wrong

Double-clicking `setup.exe` looked like it did nothing. Measured, it was doing everything: the
package unpacked, `install.cmd` ran, the toolchain was installed, and the version file was written.
What it never did was **show anything** — and the console it leaves behind is not visible in that
launch, so "installed correctly" and "nothing happened at all" were the same thing on screen. It also
left `cmd` processes sitting at `pause` afterwards.

That is worse than a cosmetic problem: the previous release's headline installer bug was a package
that silently installed nothing, so the reasonable reading of "no window appeared" was that this one
was broken too.

## What this release changes

**The installer has a face.** A window that, on a plain double-click:

1. fades in a rounded Loment mark and **Welcome to Loment**;
2. asks where to install, with the switches it used to bury in `README.md` as checkboxes
   (PATH, `.lomt`/`.lom` file association, the agent guide);
3. shows the install as it runs — the actual `install.ps1` output, streamed line by line;
4. ends on a **receipt**: a green check, `Loment 0.1.4.5 QuickFix is installed.`, and the window
   **stays open until you close it**.

It does not reimplement any of the install: it drives `install.ps1` and shows what `install.ps1`
says. One implementation of the install, two faces.

**The command line is untouched.** `install.cmd` with **any** argument (`-Prefix`, `-NoPath`,
`-DryRun`, `-Uninstall`, and everything CI uses) takes the console path it always had, with the same
output and the same exit codes. Only a bare double-click — no arguments — opens the window.

**A second, quieter fix.** The installers now resolve `loment` and `lompi` after installing and
**name** anything earlier on `PATH` that is not this install. They only ever append to `PATH`
(deliberately — an installer should not reorder a machine it does not own), so a copy installed
earlier by hand wins silently, and `lompi version` then reports the older build with nothing
anywhere explaining why.

## Install

| Asset | |
|---|---|
| `loment-0.1.4.5-quickfix-windows-x64-setup.exe` | Windows x86-64. Double-click; a window walks you through it. |
| `loment-0.1.4.5-quickfix-windows-x64.zip` | Windows x86-64. Unzip and run `install.cmd` (same window), or call `install.ps1` yourself. |
| `loment-0.1.4.5-quickfix-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64. Unchanged from 0.1.4.5 — the Linux route always printed what it was doing. |
| `loment-skill.zip` | The agent guide (`SKILL.md`) on its own. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Checksums. The installers verify the payload against this before copying anything. |

Installing and running needs **no Python, no clang and no WSL**.

## Which release to install

* **0.1.4.5's installer is unchanged and stays published as it is.** Its `setup.exe` does install —
  it just does it invisibly. If you already installed from it, you have this toolchain; nothing needs
  re-installing.
* **0.1.4's `setup.exe` is still not being rebuilt**
  ([#117](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/issues/117)) — that asset genuinely installs nothing.
  Use the `zip`, or take this release.

## Everything else

There are no other changes. What 0.1.4.5 contains — the four-rung GC ladder and the generational
collector, networking on both targets, lompi 0.2.0 Alpha — and what it does **not** contain, along
with the known open bugs, are listed in the
[0.1.4.5 release notes](https://github.com/FujoJTOP/loment/releases/tag/v0.1.4.5); that document
still stands as written.
